preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain control of owner account)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) to disable the automatic liquidity addition mechanism. This prevents the contract from converting accumulated fees to liquidity, allowing the owner to later drain accumulated tokens from the contract address. Alternatively, the owner could set the marketing/investing wallets to attacker-controlled addresses to redirect fee distributions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a privileged function setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled that can only be called by the owner. By setting this to false, the owner disables the automatic liquidity addition mechanism, which prevents accumulated fees from being converted to liquidity. This allows the owner to potentially drain accumulated tokens later. The oracle verification specifically checks that _swapAndLiquifyEnabled == false, confirming this state tampering.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) to disable the automatic liquidity mechanism, satisfying the oracle check.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner address from the contract. 2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner. 3. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(false) on the target contract. 4. Verify that _swapAndLiquifyEnabled is now false.
